Chapter 1 Introduction to LyX We will start off by understanding what LyX is an how we can use it for economic publication quality reports. We will discuss what is LyX and how we can install it onto our machine. Next, we will go through LyX’s Tutorial and use the Example document. 1.1 What you see is what you get (WYSIWYG) LaTex word processor We are able to use LaTex documents without knowing too much LaTex ourselves with LyX. We can insert LaTex code into a LyX document, but with LyX this is not necesary. We will want to understand some of the basic of LaTex, so we can incorporate mathematical equations. We will cover this in the next chapter. 1.2 Install LyX 1.2.1 Windows Installation Please see: https://wiki.lyx.org/Windows/WindowsSetup 1.2.2 OSX Installation Please see: https://www.baeldung.com/cs/lyx-installation or https://wiki.lyx.org/Mac/Mac 1.3 LyX Tutorial After we launch the LyX tutorial, we will want to open a new document. Go to File \(\rightarrow\) New or click on the following: New Document 1.3.1 Select Document Class Go to Document \(\rightarrow\) Settings. Lyx Document Settings Make sure “Article Standard Class” is selected. This will provide the sections that we need for our document. Article Standard Class Now go back to the main window and look to the upper left to see the Envionment window. It should should the word “Standard”. LyX Style Window 1.3.2 Sections After selecting “Standard” in the Environment window, go to “Section” under “Sectioning”. LyX Environment Window This will create a new section, which will look like this. Next, we can enter our section header, which will be “Introduction” for this example. LyX Numbered Section 1 Next, press “Enter” and begin to type your introduction paragraph. Introductory paragraph 1.3.3 Subsections After your introduction paragraph(s), press enter for a new paragraph. You will notice that the new paragraph is indented. We will type the word “Background” for our first subsection. It will look like the following: New paragraph indented Now go back to the Environment window and select “Subsection” under “Sectioning”. New Subsection Selection The result will be that “Background” becomes subsection 1.1. New Subsection Added We can do this several subsections. We will create “Theory” and “Literature Review” subsections. Additional subsections 1.3.4 Preview our work Now that we have created our first section. Let’s preview what our pdf will look like. Click the preview button to see the preview. Preview your work 1.3.5 Title, Author, and Abstract Let’s add a title to our article. Go to the first line and enter your title of the article. In this example, we will call the article “Econ 643 LyX Example”. Add a Title Go back to the Environment window and select “Title” under “Front Matter”. Title Option Select “Title” and your title will become a title for your article. New Title 1.3.6 Add an author Under your title, add your name. Next select “Author” under the “Front Matter” section of the Environment window. 1.3.7 Table of Contents We can add a table of contents (optional). As long as we are using sectioning, a table of contents will automatically generate once we select 1.3.8 Mathematical Equations We can click the following button to insert a mathematical equation into a LyX document. Mathematical Equation in LyX 1.3.9 Insert LaTex Results We can export our LaTex code that is produced from Stata with the estout commands. When you preview the document, you will notice that there is LaTex code that automatically labels the table number. To insert a place to insert the LaTex output from Stata, click Insert \(\rightarrow\) Tex Code. Insert Function Now you will see a new box in your Lyx Document. LaTex insert box Next paste your LaTex code output from Stata into Lyx with right-click and Paste. LaTex Right-Click Paste We will discuss estout in the next chapter. 1.3.10 Insert Figure Our final tutorial will cover inserting graphs from Stata. We will cover exporting graphs from Stata a bit later. We need to export our Stata histogram that we created. We will save it as a “.png” file. Histogram we want to insert Go to Insert \(\rightarrow\) Float \(\rightarrow\) Figure. Insert Figure Now enter a title for the figure. We will use “Histogram of Automobile Price”. Figure Title Next, we need to insert the histogram from Stata above the Figure 1: box but below Float Figure. Go to Insert \(\rightarrow\) Graphics. Insert Graphics In the Graphics window, click browse and find your histogram “.png” file. Next, select “set width” and choose the size of your choice. Next, select “Column Width %” from the drop down menu next to “set width”. Click “OK”. Graphics Window Your histogram will be inserted, but it may look funny. Inserted Histogram Click on preview to see how well the histogram was inserted. You may need to play around with the settings. I have the size of the Stata graph window makes the graphic file larger. Inserted Histogram PDF 1.4 Export Your LaTex file into PDF Go to File \(\rightarrow\) Export \(\rightarrow\) Export As. Select the location of the folder you want to store the file. Next, enter the name of the file and select “PDF (pdflatex) (*.pdf)“. Export As in LyX

Chapter 2 Introduction to LaTex I will provide a crash course on how to use LaTex to create mathematical equations. Kemp, et al. (2016) discuss how LaTeX is the “industry standard” typesetting system for writing mathematics. LaTeX is more flexible than standard word processors, such as MSWord), produces vastly better-looking results. Learning how to create mathematical equations with LaTex will help you with your homework and projects through the empirical sequence. With LaTex, we can turn y=bx^2+c into \[ y=\beta x^2 + c \] If you want a mean, you don’t have to type mu or average. Just use LaTex by entering “\ mu” which results in \(\mu\). Do you want to expected value of x? You can just use E(x), but it looks better with LaTex with \(E(x)\). 2.1 How to use mathematical symbols We typicall use the “\" to initate a mathemetical symbol. We can use”^” for superscripts and “” for subscripts. For example, we can type \ sum^N{i=1} x_{i} and it will become \[ \sum^N_{i=1} x_{i} \] You may have noticed that the subscripts had {} brackets. When we want to include an equation in the subscript or subscript, we need to include {} brackets, such as x^{2a+3b}. This will result in \(x^{2a+3b}\) 2.2 Overview of mathematical symbols I think the following is a helpful reference guide for mathematical symbols in LaTex Source: https://quickref.me/latex.html 2.3 Greek letters Source: https://quickref.me/latex.html 2.4 Accents and Braces Source: https://www.tilburgsciencehub.com/topics/research-skills/templates-dynamic-content/templates/amsmath-latex-cheatsheet/ 2.5 Binary Relations and Operators Binary Relations and Operators Source: https://www.tilburgsciencehub.com/topics/research-skills/templates-dynamic-content/templates/amsmath-latex-cheatsheet/
